messages.subject_clean: Rattle not giving same regression results as R
messages.body_plain:
On 20 June 2012 02:26, Phillip Baddour <badd...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I am a new user of Rattle. I installed Rattle version 2.6.18, using it with R version 2.15.0, on a Windows 7 64 bit computer. My data set consists of 10 rows with 4 numeric observations. If I import the data to rattle and run linear on the model tab, I get a different result compared to when I run lm from R. That result occurs either when I read the data directly into R, or when I run lm on the crs$dataset created by rattle.
>
> My data is as follows:
>                             Fund   NAV Mkt.Price Prem.Disc.. X52.Week
> 1    Alpine Glbl Prem Prop (AWP)  6.80      6.12      -10.00    -4.78
> 2  CBRE Clarion Glbl RE Inc(IGR)  8.65      7.70      -10.98     1.68
> 3  Cohen & Steers Qual Rlty(RQI) 10.59      9.86       -6.89    14.77
> 4  Cohen & Steers REIT&Pref(RNP) 17.22     15.95       -7.38     9.20
> 5    Cohen & Steers TR Rlty(RFI) 13.37     13.20       -1.27     7.23
> 6    LMP Real Estate Income(RIT) 11.56     10.17      -12.02     8.17
> 7     Neuberger RE Sec Inc(NRO)a  4.93      4.20      -14.81     7.31
> 8  Nuveen Dvs Div & Income(JDD)a 11.76     11.20       -4.76    10.39
> 9   Nuveen Real Estate Inc(JRS)a 10.28     10.50        2.14     8.55
> 10  RMR Real Estate Income(RIF)a 19.41     15.82      -18.50    -5.74

Hi Phillip,

Have a look in the Log tab - that will show the actual R commands that are run by rattle and you can then compare that to what you are doing directly in R.

Regards,
Graham

On Thursday, June 21, 2012 1:50:26 AM UTC+10, Phillip Baddour wrote:
> Thank you for your response. The commands shown in the log indicate a sample of my dataset is being used in the calculations, rather than all observations. Is there a setting I am missing which would allow the calculations to be made on all observations?

Yes. In the Data tab, turn off Partition.

Regards,
Graham
